source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 1-year Public Use Microdata Sample, person files, 2008-2024 (national, 50 states and DC)
target: Share of people who report a divorce in the past 12 months, per 1,000 people aged 15+ who were married at some point in those 12 months (currently married or separated, or divorced or widowed within the 12 months). Cross-sectional one-year incidence from a single interview, not a prospective hazard or a lifetime risk.

excluded_from_pool.2020: Census released 2020 1-year data with experimental weights

uncertainty: 95% CI = estimate +/- 1.96 SE; SE from the 80 successive-difference replicate weights; pooled years combine replicate i across years
caveats: Characteristics are measured at the interview, after any divorce: income, employment, occupation, state of residence and even education can follow the divorce rather than precede it.

Duration is years since the most recent wedding (survey year minus MARHYP); unknown for people who divorced and remarried within the same 12 months, who are all events by construction, so cells by duration leave them out (they remain in the overall rate and in cells not split by duration).
Interviews run through each calendar year, so the 12-month window straddles two calendar years.
Rates describe people, not couples: each spouse of a divorcing couple can be counted.
Cells are descriptive; pointwise CIs are not adjusted for the many comparisons.

model_predicted_risk.method: Weighted percentiles (p1..p99) of the held-out predicted probability of a divorce within one year (horizon 1), among test-set people (10% of households, pooled 2019 and 2021-2024); subgroups with fewer than 200 people omitted. Cross-sectional: inputs are measured at the interview.

age_standardised_note: Direct age standardisation to the pooled at-risk population (ages 15-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-64, 65+), computed in every replicate for the CI; published only when a cell has people in all five bands.
detail_dims_note: race_detail: Hispanic (any race), then non-Hispanic single races (RAC1P) and Multiracial (two or more races). asian_detail: non-Hispanic Asian alone by RAC2P detailed group. hispanic_origin: HISP detailed origin, small origins grouped as Central/South American. household_income_band: HINCP x ADJINC in 2024 dollars (CPI-U). tenure/owner: TEN. Income and tenure are measured at the interview, after any divorce.
